dependent_variable.name: TPRANK
dependent_variable.definition: Within-analyst rank correlation between forecasted and realized returns for stocks covered during a semi-annual period. Forecasted return is (TP−P)/P and realized return is (P12−P)/P; P is the closing price three trading days before target-price release and P12 is the price 12 months after release. Dividends are ignored in both returns.
dependent_variable.formula: For analyst a and period s, rank-correlation across covered stocks of forecast return (TP−P)/P and realized return (P12−P)/P.

evidence.quote: First, we compute the within-analyst rank correlation (TPRANK) between forecasted and realized returns for stocks covered by an analyst in a semi-annual measurement period detailed below.

Realized return for a covered stock is calculated as (P12-P)/P, where P12 is the stock price 12-months following the target price release date, and P is the closing price three trading days before the target price release date.
An analyst’s forecasted return on a covered stock is calculated as (TP-P)/P, where TP is the target price forecast.
We ignore dividends in both realized and forecasted returns for simplicity.
For TPRANK, we calculate one rank correlation for each analyst in each semi-annual period.

preprocessing.description: Target-price forecasts and actual stock prices are converted to the same split-adjusted basis. The sample excludes non-12-month horizons, observations missing the pre-release or 12-month price, share prices below $1, and extreme TP/P ratios (bottom one percent or greater than four); TPRANK additionally requires at least three target-price forecasts per analyst in a semi-annual period.

evidence.quote: We use target price forecasts and actual stock prices converted to the same split-adjusted basis.

Less: Target prices without 12-month forecast horizon (14,603)
